changes.text: 行军的账很难看。头几天里有一天，直线只前进了约一英里；为了绕开障碍，实际走过的距离至少两英里；分批搬运、来回接力，又把当天走过的路程推到了六英里，有几组狗队至少跑了十英里。那晚的营地扎在平坦但又年轻又咸的冰上。行军第一夜，虎鲸一直在喷气，凌晨2点，离营地约20英尺处裂开一道缝。他写道，脚下的冰薄得足以让虎鲸撞破，可近处没有别的地方能扎营，只好冒这个险。

The arithmetic of the march made ugly reading. On one of the first days they gained about one mile in a direct line; the detours made the ground actually covered at least two miles, and the relays pushed the day's marching up to six. Some of the dog teams had covered at least ten miles. That night they camped on flat ice that "proved to be young and salty." On the first night of the march, killer whales blew all night, and at 2 a.m. a crack opened about 20 feet from the camp. The ice was thin enough for the killers to break through, he wrote, "but there was no other camping-ground within our reach and we had to take the risk."

一种解释是（作者推断），海洋营不是他第一次决定停下。行军第二天早上，雪大得看不清路，他就决定不拔营；天晴一些后探到一块好走的浮冰，午饭后又继续走。两次决定都在衡量眼前的路还能不能走下去。扎营等待也不是新想法：在海洋营之前，他已经写下过在最近的厚浮冰上扎营、等浮冰外漂到开阔水面的方案，并说这样还能减少冰面在脚下开裂的危险。他写道，在他们的“第一个营地”，冰面曾一夜裂开两次；这段记述没有交代那是哪个营地，不能直接等同于前文所记的行军第一夜。但他确信应当先尝试行军，还特别提到这个问题有心理层面的考虑：让大家觉得自己正在朝陆地走，比坐等漂流要好。海洋营是在四天苦干之后回到这个先前暂且搁置、留作退路的方案。营地选在更结实的浮冰上，理由里挂着一个具体的指望：附近可能开出水道，那时可以划船去找陆地。等条件更有利，再做第二次尝试。

One reading, and it is the author's, is that Ocean Camp was not the first time he chose to stop. On the march's second morning, with snow too thick to see a path, he decided not to strike camp; when it cleared and a good floe turned up, they moved on after lunch. Both decisions turned on whether the way ahead could be made. Nor was camping to wait a new idea. Before Ocean Camp he had already written down the option of camping on the nearest heavy floe and awaiting the outward drift of the pack to open water, noting that it would also lessen the peril of the ice splitting under them. He wrote that at their "first camp" the ice had split twice in one night; the passage does not say which camp that was, and it should not simply be equated with the march's first night described earlier. But he felt sure it was right to attempt a march first, noting that there was a psychological aspect too: the men would be better off feeling they were on their way to land than simply sitting and waiting for the drift. Ocean Camp, after four days of hard effort, was a return to that option he had set aside. The camp went onto a more solid floe, and the reasoning carried a specific hope: leads opening nearby, boats in the water, land to the north-west. A second attempt was to follow once conditions improved.

dispositions.rationale: S-E6 的位置只标为“行军头几天”，S-E12 才是第一夜的记述。修改后，S-E6 的距离账和“年轻又咸”冰面上的营地改写为头几天中“有一天”的情况；第一夜的虎鲸、凌晨2点的裂缝和薄冰另起一句单独叙述，不再把两者标为同一天。英文同步修改。

evidence.quote: So I gave the order to pitch camp for the night on flat ice, which, unfortunately, proved to be young and salty.
The killers were blowing all night, and a crack appeared about 20 ft. from the camp at 2 a.m.

dispositions.rationale: 删去容易与行军第一夜混淆的“在第一个营地，冰面一夜裂开两次；那一夜之后”这一写法。“第一个营地”改为加引号的转述，并明确说明原文没有交代是哪个营地，不能等同于前文的行军第一夜。时间点只写到“在海洋营之前”。没有采纳建议中的“行军开始前”，因为 S-E19 原文提到“we are now incurring”的危险，证据文字本身不能确定这段写于行军之前；在海洋营之前写下，则有该段末尾的“We will make an attempt to move”为据。英文同步修改。

evidence.quote: it would also minimize the peril of the ice splitting under us, as it did twice during the night at our first camp, Yet I feel sure that it is the right thing to attempt a march
We will make an attempt to move.
